BiblicalUsage: Once, in the vision of the Ancient of Days: I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool. The word is wool itself, and the hair of the Ancient is white as the wool that has never been dyed.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for wool carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the whiteness, that the Ancient of Days is seen in the colour of purity itself.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
